## Introduction

Robot vacuums in 2026 do far more than bump around your floors. The latest models mop, scrub away stains, lift themselves over obstacles and even point out the dirtiest spots in your home. WIRED tested the newest models in a real three-story home shared by three adults, a preschooler and a cat, and picked three worth buying right now. Prices below are list prices. WIRED's September 2026 update showed the Shark at $693, the Eufy at $380 and the Roborock at $450 on sale.

## Best overall: Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal

The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal lists at $1,300 and is WIRED's top pick. Its UV light reveals spots on the floor where spills happened. Its built-in AI sends the vacuum back to deep-clean those spots. It mops and vacuums hard floors, including luxury vinyl plank and tile. It also did a good job on builder-grade carpet and a large rug. The vacuum has an extendable arm for corners. In WIRED's corner test it picked up two out of three Cheerios placed in tricky corners, doing better than the latest Dyson vacuum. It finished cleaning a four-room main floor in about 60 minutes. Then it took another 30 minutes going back to scrub the spots it found. Its auto-empty base uses a bagless debris system, so no debris bags to buy. Two limits matter. The vacuum learns only a single map, so it does not suit homes with more than one floor unless you remap each time. Shark also declined to say how much suction it produces.

## Best on a budget: Eufy Omni C28

The Eufy Omni C28 lists at $800. It is the pick if you want vacuuming and mopping without paying a four-figure sum. Eufy released it at the end of February with nearly double the suction power of the older X10 Pro Omni. It has a self-cleaning roller mop instead of mop pads, and retractable detangling brushes. It stores maps for more than one floor, but its battery is short. It was down to 37 percent after cleaning the four-room main floor. It reached 57 percent after just 20 minutes back in its docking station. It also tried to eat the cords near the reviewer's bed, so cords need to be kept clear of its reach. In the corner test it also collected two out of three Cheerios, missing the hardest fridge-corner spot. In the cherry juice spill test it cleaned the first spot completely, while the second, which had longer to dry, left some sticky residue. It is usually on sale for around $500.

## Another budget option: Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro

The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro also lists at $800. It is the newest update to Roborock's more affordable Qrevo line. It packs 20,000 Pa of suction, a FlexiArm mop that cleans corners better, and a reversible side brush to dislodge corner debris. It is cheaper than the Curv 2 that launched in January 2026 and has the same handy app. It is quieter than the Eufy, both at the base station and in the vacuum itself. It cleaned a large first floor with a separate vacuuming session and mopping session in two hours. It is not great at seeing small objects. It took the reviewer's cat's toys for rides around the room. In the Cheerio test it scored two out of three and got the harder fridge Cheerio with its FlexiArm mop. Its mopping scored 1.25 out of 2, with one spill almost gone but sticky around the edges and the second only half cleaned. It also tends to leave some debris behind when it crosses thresholds between carpet and hard flooring.

## Also worth a look

The Dreame L60 Ultra lists at $1,300 and packs 35,000 Pa of suction, dual flex arms, and an EasyLeap system that lets it move over obstacles almost 2 inches tall. That makes it a good choice if your home has tall thresholds. The Dreame X50 Ultra lists at $1,000 and suits homes with pets. It has double-roll brushes and AI that notices extremely dirty areas and reminds you which areas need cleaning more often. The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai lists at $1,200 and uses AI to find spots and stains to scrub. But it is a little tall and got stuck underneath the reviewer's Tolstad bed frame. The iRobot Roomba Max 705 Combo lists at $799 and did a good job mopping and cleaning, with an app that shows a map of where the robot went. Setup and any resetting takes a long time, though.

## How to choose

If your home has more than one floor, check that the vacuum can store more than one map. The Shark learns only a single map, while the Eufy stores maps for all three levels of a home. If you have tall thresholds between rooms, look for a model that can lift itself over them, like the Dreame L60 Ultra with its EasyLeap system. If you have pets, look for AI that spots the dirtiest areas, like the Dreame X50 Ultra. And if mopping matters most, look for a self-cleaning roller mop like the Eufy's rather than mop pads.
